Phylogenetic signal with known measurement error

Source: R/phylo-signal.R
phylo_signal.Rd

Estimates Pagel's lambda or Blomberg's K for a continuous trait, optionally accounting for known standard errors of the species means (Ives et al. 2007). It fits the same models as phytools::phylosig() with se, but evaluates the likelihood in time linear in the number of species with the three-point algorithm (Ho & Ane 2014) instead of inverting the full phylogenetic covariance matrix, so it scales to trees with many thousands of tips.

Usage

phylo_signal(
  x,
  phy,
  se = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  species = NULL,
  method = c("lambda", "K"),
  test = TRUE,
  nsim = 1000
)

Arguments

x

Trait values: a column of data (see below), or a numeric vector named by species (names matching phy$tip.label), or an unnamed one with the species given in species. Species with NA are dropped with a warning, and tips without data are pruned from the tree.

phy

A phylogeny of class "phylo" with branch lengths.

se

Optional standard errors of x, given the same way as x: a column of data, a vector named by species, or an unnamed vector in the same order as x. NULL (default) means no measurement error.

data

An optional data frame (or tibble) with one row per species. x, se and species are then looked up in its columns, as in subset() or lm(): a bare column name (x = log_mass), a string (x = "log_mass"), or an expression (x = log(mass)).

species

The species of each value of x: a column of data, or a vector as long as x. If NULL (default), the row names of data are used when it has them (a tibble never has row names, and neither does a data frame read from a file without row.names), otherwise the names of x.

method

"lambda" (default) or "K".

test

Logical. For lambda, a likelihood-ratio test against lambda = 0; for K, a randomization test that shuffles the trait values (together with their standard errors) across the tips.

nsim

Number of randomizations for the K test.

Value

An object of class "phylo_signal": a list with, for lambda, lambda, sig2, logL, and with test = TRUE logL0 (lambda = 0), LR and P; for K, K, sig2, logL (at the maximum-likelihood \(\sigma^2\), before the \(n/(n-1)\) correction; NA without se), and with test = TRUE P and sim_K. Also method and n.

Details

With measurement error, the covariance of the trait is $$V = \sigma^2 C(\lambda) + diag(se^2),$$ where \(C(\lambda)\) is the phylogenetic covariance with off-diagonal elements multiplied by \(\lambda\). For lambda, \(\sigma^2\) and \(\lambda\) are estimated by maximum likelihood with the mean profiled out by GLS; \(\lambda\) is searched on [0, maximum lambda] where the maximum keeps the covariance valid (1 for an ultrametric tree with no polytomy at the root, often slightly above 1), first on a grid and then refined, so results do not depend on random starting values.

For K, \(\sigma^2\) of \(V = \sigma^2 C + diag(se^2)\) is estimated by maximum likelihood, multiplied by \(n/(n-1)\), and K is computed from \(V\) as in Blomberg et al. (2003), following phytools::phylosig(). Without se, \(\sigma^2\) cancels and K is the usual Blomberg's K. The P-value is \((1 + \#\{K_{sim} \ge K\}) / (nsim + 1)\).

References

Blomberg S.P., Garland T. & Ives A.R. 2003. Testing for phylogenetic signal in comparative data: behavioral traits are more labile. Evolution 57, 717-745.

Ives A.R., Midford P.E. & Garland T. 2007. Within-species variation and measurement error in phylogenetic comparative methods. Systematic Biology 56, 252-270.

Ho L.S.T. & Ane C. 2014. A linear-time algorithm for Gaussian and non-Gaussian trait evolution models. Systematic Biology 63, 397-408.

Revell L.J. 2012. phytools: an R package for phylogenetic comparative biology (and other things). Methods in Ecology and Evolution 3, 217-223.

Examples

set.seed(1)
phy <- ape::rcoal(200)
dat <- data.frame(sp = phy$tip.label,
                  se = runif(200, 0.1, 0.3))
dat$mass <- as.vector(t(chol(ape::vcv(phy))) %*% rnorm(200)) + rnorm(200, 0, dat$se)

# a column of species names (also for tibbles)
phylo_signal(mass, phy, se = se, data = dat, species = sp)
#> Phylogenetic signal (200 species)
#> 
#> lambda          : 1
#> sig2            : 1.042
#> logLik          : -36.67
#> LR (lambda = 0) : 615, P < 2.2e-16
phylo_signal(mass, phy, se = se, data = dat, species = sp, method = "K", nsim = 199)
#> Phylogenetic signal (200 species)
#> 
#> K               : 2.503
#> sig2            : 1.047
#> logLik          : -36.68
#> P               : 0.005 (199 randomizations)

# species as row names
rownames(dat) <- dat$sp
phylo_signal(mass, phy, se = se, data = dat, test = FALSE)
#> Phylogenetic signal (200 species)
#> 
#> lambda          : 1
#> sig2            : 1.042
#> logLik          : -36.67

# named vectors
x <- setNames(dat$mass, dat$sp)
s <- setNames(dat$se, dat$sp)
phylo_signal(x, phy, se = s, test = FALSE)
#> Phylogenetic signal (200 species)
#> 
#> lambda          : 1
#> sig2            : 1.042
#> logLik          : -36.67
